body: The discrepancy in behaviour between a round shape and a rectangle shape colliding with an edge and a dive in the `test_body_motion` source code suggest that this phenomenom is caused by how collision normals are calculated between a round and a rectangle collider vs. between two rectangle colliders. When one-way collision is enabled on a shape, collisions will be discarded based on the angle between the collision normal and the local up axis (y axis) of the shape, which is the one-way collision direction. (Collision depth is also factored in.) In the image above, the yellow line is the plane defined by the one-way collision direction. If the collision normal (green arrow) points towards the upper side of the plane, then the collision is valid, if it is parallel or points below the plane, then it's discarded. In the case of the sphere shape colliding with the corner in the example, the normal points slightly up, so the collision is valid, but because it's steep, it's a wall collision. In the case of the rectangle, there is no such change on corners, the normal remains perpendicular to the one way collision direction, so the collision is discarded. The simplest soution: use a rectangle shape for characters. Otherwise, one thing I thought up, is maybe a customizable angle value could be factored in when comparing the normal with the one-way collision direction. I'm not sure if this is a good idea. @JohanAR Out of curiosity, is there a particular reason (or reasons) you need a round shape for characters?

Hi @DinkeyKing . I also noticed that the collision normal was the source of the is_on_wall value while digging through the code trying to see if I could work around it, however, IMO it is a bit illogical that a one-way platform can trigger in_on_wall since the tile doesn't have any walls :) And having it trigger on an internal edge while jumping through a platform definitely seems like a bug, though I suspect it could be fixed by baking the tilemap collision shape.

The reason that I'm using a capsule collider is that rectangles don't work well with slopes. A full rectangle makes the character hover in the air, while a narrow rectangle instead allows it to partially clip into walls. It also eliminates the need for edge snapping which seemed like a nice bonus. They're ofc. possible to solve, but it would be nice if rounded colliders also worked well for 2D games.

> IMO it is a bit illogical that a one-way platform can trigger in_on_wall since the tile doesn't have any walls :) And having it trigger on an internal edge while jumping through a platform definitely seems like a bug

You're right, you wouldn't expect a one-way platform to have wall collision's, but as I explained in my previous comment, one-way collisions don't exactly act like one-way platforms, at least not when using round colliders.

> though I suspect it could be fixed by baking the tilemap collision shape.

Removing the internal egdes means removing the internal corners, so it does fix those, but the outer edges still pose this problem. 

> The reason that I'm using a capsule collider is that rectangles don't work well with slopes. A full rectangle makes the character hover in the air, while a narrow rectangle instead allows it to partially clip into walls. It also eliminates the need for edge snapping which seemed like a nice bonus. They're ofc. possible to solve, but it would be nice if rounded colliders also worked well for 2D games.

Thanks for explaining! Personally, I don't like how round colliders allows characters to hang from ledges.

As I proposed before, I think being able to customize the angle threshold used for comparing the normal and the one-way direction could be a solution for this, but I also suspect it would cause characters with round shapes to drop off from ledges farther than expected, because collisions would be discarded in a broader angle. I'm not sure how to proceed with this issue.

Another possible fix that came to my mind, is that the the motion vector could also be factored in. Collisions could be discarded, if the motion vector does not face the one-way collision direction, which in this case should be the opposite direction of the surface's normal we want collisions to happen with.  But this would mean that we expect the one-way platform collider to have all its colliding edges face a single direction, which is problematic.

That said, if you're only concered about the round collider colliding with internal edges, and not the outer corners, than I guess setting up your colliders in way that avoids these problematic inner edges is also a solution.

> Personally, I don't like how round colliders allows characters to hang from ledges.

That is also something I found less than ideal, but I thought I could live with it. My game project is intended to be more of a puzzle platformer than precision. I'll probably end up writing some custom solution, I've seen a couple of different options including raycasts, multiple collision shapes, or hard-coded logic.

I was thinking that it might be possible to include the information about the tile that the object collided with, i.e. if it was a one-way platform, and then add that to the check for is_on_wall (possibly with an option, in case anyone wants to keep the current behaviour)
This is affected by TileMap chunking https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102662 now the unintended behaviour, appears to only happen on chunk edges.
